title: Prospective investigation of intraoperative changes in CMAP amplitude and safety of repeated neuromuscular stimulation under general anesthesia
summary:
During surgery under general anesthesia, many patients receive medications that temporarily relax the muscles. To monitor the effect of these drugs, the response of the muscles to small electrical impulses is routinely measured.

This method has been used for many years and is considered safe. However, it has not been systematically investigated to what extent repeated measurements during surgery may influence the recorded values or the surrounding tissue. In particular, it remains unclear whether observed changes reflect true alterations in nerve or muscle function or are caused by technical or external factors.

The aim of this study is to systematically investigate these changes and to further assess the safety and reliability of the measurement method.

For this purpose, standardized measurements will be performed on both hands during anesthesia. One hand will be stimulated repeatedly as part of routine clinical monitoring, while the other hand will serve as a comparison. In addition, brief pre- and postoperative assessments of the skin, sensation, and motor function of the hand will be conducted.

The study is intended to improve the understanding of neuromuscular monitoring during anesthesia and to contribute to patient safety in the long term.
conditions: Investigation of neuromuscular function and potential changes in muscle, nerve, and skin associated with intraoperative neuromuscular monitoring under general anesthesia in patients undergoing elective surgery.

interventions.name:
Arm 1: Single-arm prospective observational study with intraindividual comparison

Adult patients undergoing elective surgery under general anesthesia with neuromuscular blockade will be included.
Intraoperative neuromuscular monitoring is performed routinely using peripheral nerve stimulation. W

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Elective surgery under general anesthesia (duration 4-10 hrs)
Use of a non-depolarizing neuromuscular blocking agent (rocuronium) as part of anesthesia management
Exclusion criteria:
• Neuromuscular disorders
• Known peripheral neuropathies
• Finger contractures
• Skin diseases affecting the electrode area
• Indication for ileus induction
• Implanted electrical systems (e.g., active neurostimulator)
• Allergy to rocuronium
• Pregnancy
• Patient refusal to participate in the study
• Concurrent participation in another study
• Limited capacity to provide informed consent, including care needs
